newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary says real wages to fall up to 4pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Hungary says real wages to fall up to 4pct in 1996.

text.p: Hungary's finance minister Peter Medgyessy said on Monday he expected real wages to fall by three to four percent in 1996.
"Real wages have decreased by 16 to 17 percent in the past two years and I expect them to fall by three to four percent this year," he told the Hungarian International Press Association.
The government originally expected real wages to fall by two percent in 1996 and signed an agreement on that basis with employees and unions to avert industrial action.
Medgyessy said the higher figure was due to a revised inflation figure for 1996 of 22-24 percent instead of the planned 20 percent.
Medgyessy said he opposed the signing of a new agreement with unions at the end of 1996.
"Personally I am against price-wage agreements with employers and employees," he said.

"I don't see a chance of us doing it as it will stoke inflation. Our intention is to keep real wages at their current level, but it is only an intention. The guarantee lies in the performance of the economy."
